Bryson DeChambeau was at the centre of controversy after being hit with a two-stroke penalty after his second round at The Open at Royal Birkdale.

The Press Association’s Andy Hampson followed the American during his third round as he attempted to put the issue behind him and reignite his challenge for the Claret Jug on Saturday.

Here is how the round unfolded.

open image in gallery Bryson DeChambeau embraces spectators on his way to the second tee (Jacob King/PA). ( PA Wire )

Hole 1: The reception DeChambeau received as he arrived on the first tee was only positive, with huge cheers and shouts from the packed grandstand. The American is a hugely popular figure with a large section of the golfing public and fans were rallying behind their man. Friday’s fiasco had clearly not damaged his sense of humour too much. After carving his tee shot into the rough on the left, he bent down to remove some pine cones near his ball. “Loose impediments!” he was quick to exclaim, to much laughter from those watching.

Hole 2: The good vibes initially continued as he cracked a perfect drive down the middle of the fairway, with plenty of shouts of “Come on Bryson” as he walked to his ball. Then came the first test as his approach landed in grass similar in length to that that caused his problems. “Mind where you stand lad,” shouted one helpful Scouser before a football-style “oooooo” chant as if DeChambeau’s practice swing was a goal-kick. The resulting chip was fine, but there were groans when the par putt was missed.

Hole 3: For all the media focus on DeChambeau, it was clear by now that for this particular crowd there were bigger shows elsewhere on the course, chiefly local favourite Tommy Fleetwood. Yet, while the numbers following his all-American game with Sam Burns were thinning out, those watching continued to show their love, notably when he holed for par.

Hole 4: All the shouts of “Come on Bryson” around the green briefly turned to cries of anguish when his birdie putt stopped short but quickly resumed again. A lone voice humorously provided some variety by shouting “Come on Burnsy” instead. Burns responded with a birdie and it was him providing the early fireworks in this match.

open image in gallery Bryson DeChambeau sizes up a putt on the third green (Jacob King/PA). ( PA Wire )

Hole 5: The shout of “Up the Toffees” may have gone over his head, but it was a frustrating visit to the fifth green as a birdie opportunity went by. Still, healthy applause as he tidied up for par.

Hole 6: After more banter with fans after hitting left, there came the first signs of juices starting to flow as DeChambeau holed a lengthy, curling putt for birdie. He fist-pumped the air in delight and the fans loved it. “Get in,” a few shouted.

Hole 7: It was ‘Burnsy’ who earned the bigger cheers on this par three after coming within a whisker of a hole-in-one. DeChambeau had to settle for par, but the fans were happy enough and he high-fived a number of them on his way to the eighth tee.

Hole 8: DeChambeau had a long chat with Burns as they walked down the fairway together, but he was still struggling to match his partner. Burns birdied to move into the outright lead, but he could only par. A lone quip of “Faldo was right, your strategy’s *****” went unheard, but a chant of “Bryson, give us a wave” was obliged.

Hole 9: The fans at the ninth tee were the first to really resemble a football crowd, urging him get out his driver. He theatrically kept them waiting, letting the “oooooo” build before pulling the requested club out of his bag to huge cheers. He smacked to within yards of the green and chipped on to it but could not make birdie and the cheers turned to groans.

Hole 10: He was back in the long grass again after a wayward tee shot, but, on an isolated part of the course, there was no fan interaction this time. He missed the green, but an attempt to chip in brought applause before he holed for another par.

Hole 11: More cheers as the driver came out again, but the tee shot went left, leaving an awkward approach. It did not prevent him finding the green, but his long birdie putt turned away from the hole. There was a collective sigh.

Hole 12: On a quieter part of the course, DeChambeau was in the bunker off the tee. He recovered well to save par, fist-pumping as the ball dropped.

President Donald Trump once frequently targeted Jimmy Carter, using the 39th president as a symbol of Democratic fecklessness to bolster his own image of strength.

But Trump’s perspective on Carter has recently grown more reflective, as he confronts challenges reminiscent of those faced by the late president. These include an ongoing conflict in Iran, which shows no signs of abating and is now escalating as the U.S. seeks to control the Strait of Hormuz.

Additionally, inflation continues to burden the economy, a problem Trump has yet to resolve despite his repeated assurances that his business acumen would eliminate it.

The comparison appears to be on Trump’s mind. Last month, when questioned about why he hadn't deployed U.S. Special Forces into Iran to forcibly remove its enriched uranium, he responded, "I didn’t feel like being Jimmy Carter."

While inflation plagued both presidents, Carter had it much worse, facing a peak inflation rate of 14.7% in April 1980 ( AP Photo )

This remark harked back to the failed 1980 mission to free U.S. hostages, which resulted in the deaths of eight American servicemen. Trump also commented in March that the unsuccessful operation "cost them the election" against Ronald Reagan in 1980, indicating a newfound awareness of political realities, a departure from his earlier use of Carter as a mere punchline.

This shift in tone coincides with Trump’s increased focus on his personal legacy, as the parallels between the two presidencies become increasingly difficult to overlook.

"I think it is dawning on him — it’s getting through even his thick skull — that he’s kicked over a hornet’s nest and his presidency might be remembered for some of the same things Jimmy Carter’s presidency is," said Jonathan Alter, author of His Very Best: Jimmy Carter, A Life.

Despite some similarities, the two had glaring differences

Asked about Trump's change in tone on Carter and the two facing overlapping challenges, White House spokesperson Olivia Wales said, “Trump will never allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon” and “remains laser-focused on implementing his proven economic agenda to lower costs.”

“The president is a one-of-a-kind leader who will always unapologetically advance America’s interests," Wales said in a statement. "The only legacy he is concerned with is making America greater than ever before.”

Kori Schake, a former member of George W. Bush’s National Security Council, said she doesn't think Trump is reassessing Carter. “He doesn’t stitch facts together and create theories," she said.

Still, Trump's more recent comments are a long way from his 2024 reelection campaign, when he routinely called Joe Biden “the worst” president who made Carter look “brilliant” by comparison. Trump still frequently mentions Carter, who died two years ago at age 100, but usually to incorrectly suggest that he was wary of mail-in ballots.

Other disparities between the two are legion.

Carter was married to his wife, Rosalynn, for 77 years, was deeply religious and pledged to “never knowingly lie to the American people.” Trump is twice divorced, relishes cursing publicly and offers a never-ending onslaught of falsehoods.

As president, Carter placed his family's peanut business in a blind trust. Control of the Trump Organization has transferred to Trump's sons, but the president took in nearly $1.2 billion from his crypto businesses last year while not being shy about turning his presidency into a major source of personal benefit in other ways.

Speaking in 1977, Carter declared, “We are now free of that inordinate fear of communism.” Trump has seized on primary wins by progressive Democrats to constantly stoke new fears about communism.

Carter also won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2002. Trump hasn't, despite declaring himself more deserving than any of the award's past recipients.

The two have inflation and Iran in common

While inflation plagued both presidents, Carter had it much worse, facing a peak inflation rate of 14.7% in April 1980. Consumer prices rose 4.2% this May from a year earlier — a three-year high — and though they fell sharply from May to June, that decline included lower gas prices fueled by a U.S.-Iran ceasefire. That deal is now in tatters, driving up oil prices again.

Trump suggested he didn't think about Americans' financial woes when it comes to Iran, a war he started in conjunction with Israel in February. More recently, he shrugged off inflation concerns. But resolution has proved tricky and U.S. attacks have intensified anew after Iran's attacks on commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

Like Trump, Carter was also bedeviled by the strait, declaring during his 1980 State of the Union address that the situation “demands the participation of all those who rely on oil from the Middle East and who are concerned with global peace and stability.”

Another Trump-Carter parallel was the Democrat having considered military action to seize Kharg Island, though he ultimately decided against it so as not to jeopardize the hostages. Trump targeted the island with U.S. strikes early in the war, looking to thwart Iranian oil exports, and has threatened it again.

Schake, a senior fellow and director of foreign and defense policy studies at the American Enterprise Institute, noted a key difference was “while the Carter administration gave serious consideration to attacking Kharg Island, the reason they didn’t do it was they didn’t want to be at war with Iran."

"And we’re already at war with Iran,” she said.

Alter said Iran tried to hurt Carter's reelection chances and raised the possibility that they may do the same to Trump's Republican Party ahead of the November midterm elections.

“These people are master diplomats, and they proved that during the Carter administration," Alter said. "They’re proving that again. They’re really good at rope-a-dope.”

Trump now talks up presidential history

The president has lately name-checked many of his predecessors, praising William McKinley's support for tariffs and Teddy Roosevelt as a “great he-man.”

Trump said a key reason for reaching the now-imperiled June ceasefire with Iran was to avoid the “economic catastrophe" that befell Herbert Hoover.

“I’m a student of a lot of history,” Trump said this week.

During his first term, Trump frequently compared his own populist streak to Andrew Jackson's. He still praises Jackson but has more recently extolled many past presidential records, including those of Democrats like Franklin Delano Roosevelt.

Trump even listed some of Carter's accomplishments on the “Walk of Fame” he installed along the White House Colonnade despite displays for other Democrats, such as Barack Obama and Biden, offering biting attacks.

“Trump is thinking of his legacy, and he might have thought that attacking Iran would have enhanced it. But, in fact, it will seriously hurt,” James P. Pfiffner, a professor emeritus at George Mason University and author of several books including “The Character Factor: How We Judge Our Presidents,” said via email.

After his presidency, Alter said, Carter asked Trump for a donation to help build Carter's presidential library. Trump later wrote that Carter wanted $5 million, but he didn't answer him.

Then, during Trump's first term, Carter wrote the president a letter and Trump called to thank him, eventually leaving Carter with the impression that he might serve as a special envoy to China — an offer that never actually materialized.

“If he had learned anything from Carter’s experience — and listened to predictions about the Strait of Hormuz — he would have hesitated," Pfiffner said of war with Iran. “But he ignored lessons of history and geography.”

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s administration is actively debating whether the city has the legal power to detain Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu when he arrives for the U.N. General Assembly in September.

The potential arrest remains under discussion despite questions over municipal authority, as reported by The New York Times. Mamdani, who said that was something he would consider on the campaign trail for mayor last year, revealed that he was currently consulting with the city’s Law Department to determine his options.

“Whatever the law allows me to do in New York City, that’s what we will do, but we won’t be writing our own laws to that end,” Mamdani said during an interview on the NYT show The Interview.

“I believe that Prime Minister Netanyahu belongs in The Hague,” Mamdani told interviewer Lulu Garcia-Navarro, referencing the Netherlands city that hosts the International Court of Justice.

“He’s a war criminal who has been charged by the International Criminal Court. And what you will find is that is an opinion that is held by many, purely because of what his actions have wrought over these last many years.”

open image in gallery New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani says his administration is debating whether the city has the legal power to detain Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu when he arrives for the UN General Assembly ( Getty Images )

The stance marks a slight shift from Mamdani’s mayoral campaign last year, when he said he would directly order the New York Police Department to detain the Israeli leader. Mamdani stated at the time that the action would honor an arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court over Netanyahu’s execution of the war in Gaza, a conflict Mamdani and a United Nations commission have labeled a genocide.

Netanyahu dismissed the threats during a recent appearance with local radio host Sid Rosenberg, a frequent critic of the mayor. The prime minister rejected the remarks and countered by accusing Mamdani of harboring sympathy for Hamas, the militant group that launched the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks against Israel.

“I think he should look at who he's condemning, who he’s praising," Netanyahu told Rosenberg. “He’s condemning Israel, the one democracy that stands shoulder to shoulder with American values. Who does he champion? Hamas, that calls openly to massacre every Jew on earth, that conducted that horrible massacre, the worst massacre on Jews since the Holocaust.”

He added that Mamdani “doesn’t care” that “those who hate the Jews and Israel ultimately hate America.”

“I think, secretly, he hates America,” Netanyahu said of the mayor.

open image in gallery The Israeli prime minister dismissed the potential threat during a local radio appearance, accusing the New York City mayor of harboring sympathy for Hamas ( Getty Images )

Israel's ambassador to the United Nations, Danny Danon, also criticized the mayor on Saturday, issuing a statement that accused Mamdani of ignoring local antisemitism.

“Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu will come to New York, address the United Nations General Assembly with pride, and stand before the world to state Israel’s truth and its unwavering right to defend its citizens,” Danon said.

Mamdani, who has previously condemned the Oct. 7 attacks, as reported by CBS News, has integrated Palestinian liberation deeply into his political platform. His positions reflect broader shifts within the Democratic Party.

Earlier this week, nearly half of the House Democrats voted to halt U.S. aid to Israel. Though the measure ultimately failed, Mamdani pointed to recent local primary victories by his endorsed candidates as evidence that voters were highly motivated by the crisis.

“It is hard to find a more bankrupt policy approach than what our country has done to Gaza and to Palestine,” Mamdani said.

News.title: Wales pointless in seven-try defeat by South Africa
News.content:
The most remarkable thing about Rassie Erasmus’s Springboks is that they make total and utter dominance seem mundane.

Wales were pulverised in nearly every facet of the game but will be relieved to escape Kings Park without a repeat of the 73-0 hiding they suffered in Cardiff eight months ago. Had South Africa’s handling been just average, they would have blown past that scoreline, but the sloppy Springboks committed 20 turnovers and made 16 visits to the Wales 22 for their seven tries.

All in all, Erasmus may rate this a D- performance but it was still a good day when he was able to give four players their debuts, including fly-half Vusi Moyo, who played precisely how you would expect a 20-year-old with 58 minutes of senior rugby to perform on the Test stage.

Still, South Africa could have picked a competition winner from Durban’s party crowd to pull on the No 10 shirt and they would have still won by 30 points such was the superiority of their pack. Back-rower Paul de Villiers, who only made his debut in this summer’s Nations Championship replacing captain Siya Kolisi, is already looking like their next superstar in waiting.

If one image summed up South Africa’s complete control, it was in the 12th minute when Wales had a scrum on their own five-metre line. When the Springbok shove came, the Welsh pack went backwards like they were on roller-skates. The poor Welsh front row are going to have to check under their beds for snarling Springboks props for quite a few sleepless nights to come.

Wales’ best period of the game came just after the Springboks’ fourth try when they had three line-outs and took three tap penalties deep inside the South Africa 22. It amounted to absolutely nothing.

You can point fingers at head coach Steve Tandy’s selections and preparation if you wish, but there was little he could have done to change the result. It was only the manner of their hammering, he could have potentially affected.

Wales are not alone in this. Scotland and England may have posed a few more problems but they were still dispatched with ease. South Africa are truly in a league of their own, although New Zealand’s resurgence under Dave Rennie should at least provide a serious level of competition that the British mainland failed to provide.

In truth the best thing that Tandy could do is burn the tapes and hope that this is consigned to the deepest recesses of their collective memory. Tighthead Dillon Lewis especially may need one of those Man in Black memory wipers.

If you squinted hard enough, there were a couple of positives: the maul defence and high ball contest. The maul defence and high ball contest were at least competitive. Aaron Wainwright had the unenviable job of packing down at the back of a retreating Welsh scrum but did a heroic job in the circumstances. Jac Morgan too was bravery personified in attacking the breakdown with the ferocity of the Springboks clean-out operation.

But in the infrequent periods when South Africa got on a roll without knocking on, there was precious little Wales could do to stop the green wave. The first try was a case in point. Emanating from a loose kick from Tomos Williams, full-back Aphelele Fassi broke the first line of Wales defence and then they kept coming through Cobus Wiese, Damien de Allende before Jasper Wiese accelerated through Morgan’s tackle and over the line.

At one point, South Africa were averaging a preposterous six metres per carry and only a desperate scrambling tackle from Mee prevented Cobus Wiese from following his brother over the try line. After the Springbok front row committed an X-rated crime on their Welsh counterparts, scrum-half Cobus Reinach picked up from the resulting five-metre scrum and arced his way over in typical fashion.

His half-back partner Moyo had a very uneven game but on halftime showed the vision to crosskick to Kurt-Lee Arendse who tapped back to centre Jesse Kriel for an easy score. More punishment was to come straight out of the changing rooms. Another poor Williams kick allowed Wiese to win the tap back. A quick exchange of passes with Reinach later and Jaco Williams was over for a debut try.

The impressive Williams turned provider to put replacement scrum-half Herschel Jantjies over for the Springboks’ fifth try. Manie Libbok provided a lot more control when he came on at fly half for Moyo and it was his long mispass that allowed Arendse to register the sixth try. The outstanding De Villiers rounded off the rout with a maul try.

To think four years ago, Wales came within a whisker of pulling off a series victory in South Africa. Now they are operating in different universes entirely.

News.title: Santos impresses in first Man Utd appearance but cannot prevent defeat by Wrexham
News.content:
United were without the players who have featured at this summer’s World Cup – including new signing Youri Tielemans – as well as Benjamin Sesko, but Michael Carrick put out a strong starting XI in front of 20,000 spectators in the Finnish capital.

Santos, who became United’s first summer signing when he joined from Chelsea at the start of the week for an initial £48m, took his place at the base of midfield alongside Mason Mount.

Speaking just before the match, Michael Carrick had praised the 22-year-old’s attitude, saying: “He’s settled in really well, he’s a fantastic character. He’s buzzing to be here, you can see that.”

The Brazilian’s first involvement was to clear the ball away after Tom Heaton failed to gather under pressure from Smith seconds into the game.

Santos was left on his backside by Lewis O’Brien eight minutes in but the chance came to nothing for Wrexham as the flag went up. More encouraging was his sliding block on O’Brien moments later and he soon settled in, showing a good range of passing and winning several duels in a busy display.

However, Phil Parkinson’s side, who played their first pre-season friendly against Wisla Krakow in Poland last weekend, were looking brighter and threatened again when Bailey Cadamarteri nicked the ball off Ayden Heaven on the edge of the box before the defender recovered.

United’s first chance was a Joshua Zirkzee shot that fizzed wide in the 24th minute and they almost went ahead when Smith tried to clear a cornerm but instead sent a header on to his own crossbar in the 36th minute.

News.title: Antonelli storms to Belgian GP pole with Russell in fourth
News.content:
Kimi Antonelli raced to an emphatic pole position for Sunday’s Belgian Grand Prix to leave his world championship rivals trailing in his wake.

The 19-year-old Mercedes driver headed into qualifying as the man to beat after topping two of the three practice sessions in Spa-Francorchamps and he delivered on his status with a brilliant lap. Antonelli saved his very best to last to see off Red Bull driver Max Verstappen by 0.317 seconds.

Lando Norris qualified third, four tenths down on Antonelli, but the world champion will line up from 13th as he serves a 10-place grid penalty for exceeding his allocated number of engine parts.

“It is great to be on pole,” said Antonelli. “It was not a straightforward session, but we were able to improve lap by lap. Tomorrow is another day, but I have Max starting behind me so it is imperative to get a good start and lead into turn five. It is going to be fun tomorrow.”

Norris said: “It is not nice knowing I have to go back 10 places on the grid and that is unfortunate, but we made the most of it and I have been happy with my performance all weekend. Hopefully we can have a good race tomorrow and make up some positions. That’s the plan.”

News.title: Scotland fight back to claim victory against Fiji in Nations Championship
News.content:
Scotland round off their summer Nations Championship campaign with a game against Fiji at Murrayfield, although strictly speaking this is an official away game for Scotland. These sides met last summer in Suva, with Fiji winning 29-14. The last time these nations met at Murrayfield was two years ago, when Scotland beat Fiji 57-17.

Following their win in Argentina on the opening weekend, Scotland then made the trip to Pretoria to take on the back-to-back world champions South Africa. Gregor Townsend’s side threatened an incredible comeback at Loftus Versfeld but fell short, losing 42-28 and taking just the one bonus point home with them.

“I think that is the nature of the game [high-scoring, attacking games],” head coach Townsend said. “France won the [Six Nations] championship having conceded 96 points in the last two weekends. And they were the best team in the Six Nations. The game is in a period right now where attacks are proving too much for defences at times and that is a positive part of the game. I think there is a bit of context in our France and Argentina games in that the tries were scored near the end, where we were still encouraging our players to play, which is the mindset we want. But we would obviously like to reduce the points scored against us and increase the points that we score.

News.title: All Blacks hand Ireland brutal lesson in Nations Championship thrashing
News.content:
New Zealand welcome Ireland to the historic Eden Park in round three of the Nations Championship, with both sides taking a 100% record into this encounter. Eden Park is one of the biggest fortresses if not the biggest in world rugby, with New Zealand unbeaten on this ground in 52 consecutive Tests, with their last defeat there coming all the way back in 1994 against France.

Ireland have won just twice on 15 visits to New Zealand, with both of those victories coming on their tour to New Zealand four years ago in 2022 when they won the three-match series after victories in Dunedin and Wellington. Since then, New Zealand have won the last three meetings, including the 2023 World Cup quarter-final in Paris.

New Zealand made it two wins from two last weekend. After an enthralling, narrow win over France in the opening round, they then cruised to a 47-17 victory over Italy in Wellington seven days ago.

“Ireland have been one of the best sides in the world for a number of years now,” New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie said. “They are very experienced and well-coached and will have belief on the back of their recent success here. We are well aware of the challenge they pose. We have selected a strong team that allows some of the combinations we have tested to continue building, and rewards players who have impressed over the last two rounds, including some of our recent debutants. We know how important our bench will be against a team as tenacious as Ireland, so have selected players who we know are capable of making an impact and influencing the course of the game.”

Following a high-scoring win over Australia in Sydney on the opening weekend, Ireland then made it back-to-back victories with a 36-20 win over Japan. Those two wins mean that Ireland head into round three of the Nations Championship with a maximum 10 points out of 10. They come into this game off the back of six straight wins, with their last defeat coming in the opening round of the Six Nations against France back in February. They could jump above New Zealand into second in the world rankings with a win.

News.title: Bryson DeChambeau threatened to quit Open after two-shot penalty
News.content:
Grant Moir, the R&A executive director of governance, explained the decision. “Bryson has been penalised two strokes for inadvertently improving the area of his intended backswing on the fifth when he was playing his second shot,” he said. “Ruling one restricts what a player may do to improve any of the protected conditions affecting the stroke, and this includes the area of the player’s intended swing. So an improvement means to alter one or more of the conditions affecting the stroke so that the player gains a potential advantage for the stroke.

“Now, I’ll stress that this applies even when the action is accidental, as it was in Bryson’s case.

“The area of intended swing includes the entire area that might reasonably affect any part of the backswing, the downswing or the completion of the swing for the intended stroke.

“What the prohibited action here is that any player must not move bend or break any growing or attached or natural object. A player is allowed to fairly take their stance by taking reasonable actions to get to the ball and take a stance if, in some situations, that improves the conditions affecting the stroke.

“But when doing so the player must take the least intrusive course of action to deal with the particular situation, and is not entitled to a normal stance or swing.”

Controversial ruling splits opinion

The issue will rumble on, particularly as there are mixed opinions over whether DeChambeau was harshly treated. Wayne Riley, the former DP World Tour winner turned Sky analyst, said he was “very surprised” by the ruling. “I can’t see how Bryson is going to get penalised without a camera behind him,” he said.

Graeme McDowell concurred. “In any situation you are permitted to walk into the ball as per normal,” he said. “Clearly there are times when you have to do it with caution, like when potential branches could be broken and long fescue like this. Definitely a grey area.”

Peter Kostis, the well-known coach, also sided with DeChambeau. “In my opinion, with the depth of field issues with TV cameras and no definitive camera angles of his swing path, there cannot be conclusive video evidence that Bryson improved his lie or swing path,” he said. “In cases like this the benefit of doubt should go to the player. I don’t like this decision.”

Paul McGinley, the former Ryder Cup captain and Golf Channel analyst, took the opposite view. “The first five seconds when he got to the ball, that’s when the breach happened,” he said. “He walked up, he saw his lie, and his first thing to do then was to stand behind the ball. And in standing behind the ball, he bedded down the grass behind it, which in turn was going to improve his backswing. So for me, it’s a clear breach.”

That was how Brandel Chamblee, McGinley’s colleague, also saw it. “There were multiple infractions,” he said. “He just danced all over the path behind the golf ball. I mean, he did everything but lay down behind it or take a weed whacker to the tall grass behind it. Absolutely clear. I don’t really know what he was arguing about.”

Naturally, this overshadowed an enthralling day. Not only did Herbert equal the score for the lowest round shot in a major, but Sam Burns as well, who is alongside DeChambeau on five under.

News.title: Wall Street plunges in AI ‘bloodbath’
News.content:
The US stock market sank on Friday in a “bloodbath” for companies linked to the AI boom.

Shares on Wall Street fell heavily in the wake of sharp downturns in Japan and Taiwan as investors raised questions about the soaring valuations of companies tied to the technology.

Chip manufacturers were hit hardest after a blistering rally earlier in the year driven by surging demand.

The Nasdaq Composite, which is dominated by tech companies, plunged by 1.9pc in its sharpest fall in a month.

Kei ‌Okamura, portfolio manager at financial adviser Neuberger ‌Berman, said: “The word ‘bloodbath’ is accurate because it is across the board.”

Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 sank 4pc on Friday, having declined more than 10pc since its record high on June 25.

Sports.title: ‘I have great expectations’ – Andrey Santos leaves Man Utd fans impressed as he shines on debut vs Wrexham

Santos was the man of the hour as he was handed his first start under Michael Carrick against Championship side Wrexham.

Sports.title: Man Utd 0 Wrexham 1: United’s first pre-season game ends in major controversy as referee is BOOED off after shock defeat
Sports.content:
THE referee was BOOED off the pitch in Man United’s opening pre-season friendly that saw them lose 1-0 to the Hollywood backed Wrexham in Finland.

There were screams of a penalty from the 20,0069 crowd in the dying minutes of the 1-0 loss as Dan Gore went over in the box.

And the partisan Man United support in Scandanavia unloaded on the referee after the final whistle for not giving the decision.



Andrey Santos also made his debut in the slim defeat, but it was a former academy star that came back to haunt Michael Carrick‘s men.



Manchester-born Sam Smith‘s breakthrough secured another script-ready win for the Welcome to Wrexham cameras, but the match finished in a cloud of controversy as the referee was booed off the pitch.

It’s safe to say this is one result United’s editors will gladly leave on the cutting room floor for their own upcoming Amazon All or Nothing series.

Michael Carrick went full strength with the first half line-up, with new £50m man Santos the man of the hour.

The 22-year-old midfielder endured a shaky opening exchange, twice coughing up possession in dangerous areas and leaving Tom Heaton’s goal thoroughly exposed.



The first real flashpoint arrived soon after when Santos became embroiled in a row with Smith, accusing the former United academy star of an overly physical challenge.

Ultimately, it was Smith—who was released by United back in 2014—who earned the final bragging rights, ghosting in at the back post to tap home Lewis O’Brien’s cross and break the deadlock.

Santos soon settled and brought a rough edge and defensive discipline as United’s No6.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But Carrick’s stronger XI in the first half only mustered up one real chance when Mason Mount‘s inswinging corner was inadvertently headed against his own bar by Smith.



Alongside Youri Tielemans, Santos is two of likely three new midfield signings as Carrick revamps his side in light of Casemiro‘s exit and Manuel Ugarte‘s serious knee injury.

Both managers changed their entire line-ups for the second-half, with United’s kids up against another strong Wrexham string.

Carrick’s youngsters controlled the tempo against Wales international Kiffer Moore, midfielder Ollie Rathbone and former Wolves defender Conor Coady.



But the Carrington group hardly tested backup Wrexham keeper Danny Ward.

Carrick front loaded his first half line-up, while Wrexham manager Phil Parkinson offered two balanced line-ups to take back-to-back preseason victories over United following the Welsh side’s 3-1 win in San Diego in 2023.

Sports.title: New York hit with rare ‘dangerous and life-threatening’ emergency weather alert just hours before World Cup final
Sports.content:
NEW YORK has been hit with a rare ‘dangerous and life-threatening’ emergency weather alert just HOURS before the World Cup final.

Argentina are preparing to take on Spain in the final at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium on Sunday afternoon.



The state of New York and New Jersey has been subject to severe weather conditions in recent days due to the hundreds of wildfires burning across Canada.

A report showed that the air in New Jersey was rated ⁠as “unhealthy for sensitive groups” on Thursday.



There had already been calls to move the World Cup final due to these smoky clouds hanging over.

And now in a dramatic twist the World Cup final could be in further peril due to an emergency flash flood warning.



Certain citizens of New York City received the following emergency alert to their phones at around 12.33 pm EDT.

“National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 3.30pm EDT,” it read.

“This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.”

Regardless of the ultimate outcome to the World Cup Final taking place, it has caused utter chaos for Spain and Argentina’s final preparations.



Argentina were due to take to the practice field at the Red Bulls Performance Center in Morristown, New Jersey at 11.30am EDT.

A major thunderstorm hit the area just before their scheduled start time and delayed their training by 45 minutes.

However, they did eventually get out on the pitch, while Spain were unable to altogether.



The Spain national team was due to begin their final training session at 11 a.m. in Whippany, New Jersey at the former training training complex of the New York Red Bulls.

Ultimately, however, the adverse weather conditions proved too significant for them to partake in training, leading to it being cancelled.

That is not to say that Argentina have solely benefitted from having better weather conditions.



Lionel Scaloni’s side had their flight from their Kansas City base to New Jersey delayed by weather.

The manager claimed to the media the team had to cut short their training session on Friday to attend the pre-match press conference.

Scaloni said on Friday, “We didn’t have that much time to train because we arrived at 11pm on Thursday night.

“We had to cut the training session short because we had to come here for the press conference.

“So, tomorrow’s training session will be important to talk to them and see how they are feeling, but in theory, everyone is fit.”



New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani has issued a public update on social media for the public to take heed of.

It read, “Severe thunderstorms are hitting across New York City, and much of the city is under a flood advisory.

“Don’t risk your safety in these dangerous conditions. – Exercise caution while traveling. Take public transit whenever possible. Never walk, bike, or drive through floodwaters.

“If rain and storms are severe, seek shelter indoors and wait for conditions to improve before traveling.

Sports.title: Premier League icon reveals why England are unable to end World Cup pain as he tells Thomas Tuchel to copy Spain formula
Sports.content:
ENGLAND failed to win the World Cup because of their mentality and football culture, which extended their 60 years of hurt.

That’s according to Spain legend Gaizka Mendieta, who believes England can learn from his own national team’s winning formula, which helped them beat the Three Lions in the final of Euro 2024.



The Three Lions crashed out in the semi-finals after a late collapse that saw them surrendering their lead by sitting back and losing 2-1 to bitter rivals Argentina.

Thomas Tuchel’s men are now set to face France in the third-place play-off tonight at the Hard Rock Stadium in Miami, Florida while Lionel Messi and co go on to defend their world title against European champions Spain.



Spain will get their chance to win their second World Cup on Sunday at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, which would add to their trophy haul that also includes three Euro titles since 2008.

And Mendieta, 52, points out at the Roja’s ability to defend with the ball while controlling possession without sitting back inside the box, which is a mentality deeply rooted within the country’s football philosophy.



The former Middlesbrough star added that academies need to focus on teaching young players how to understand English football.

That is because each Premier League team has a different philosophy, but a similar youth development would allow players to build strong and quick chemistry when playing for the national team.

The Valencia legend gives immense credit to Spanish academies as their ability to ingrain the country’s style to every talented youngster has led to a strong Roja despite LaLiga clubs adopting different styles.

Mendieta told SunSport on behalf of Bovada World Cup Odds: “It’s mentality, and it’s cultural – and it’s how to play these games. You see how Spain win. It’s difficult to imagine them losing if they start winning.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

“The way we play is difficult to expect losing games like that [England’s semi-final against Argentina]. I think it’s the mentality, the way you administrate when you’re winning. It’s not putting six defenders. It’s more to that than just the physicality.

“Well, obviously, for me, one thing is cultural – the way Spain understand football professionally. But also from grassroots and academy coaching, understanding what the game needs and actually putting into place.

“I remember I was covering the Euros final, and England at some point seemed like they did not want or know how to have possession of the ball.

“And obviously Spain understood the game and started to get in passes in between and managed to win in the end. So I think again, it’s understanding how to win games, how to play games.



“These things we learn from kids, and wherever you play, whatever you do, we know how to do these things. I think England still have somehow in mind the need to defend with 11 players. It’s not like that. You can defend like we see Spain. You defend with the ball.

“You don’t need to have ten guys in the box defending. You might just keep possession. So, yeah, I think it’s these kinds of things that games require to win in the end.

“But to make the most of it, it requires learning from your academy and then the coaching as well. I think it is very important. But it’s also the clubs in England. Every club has a philosophy and an idea and way of playing.

“Similar to Spain, Real Madrid and Barcelona don’t play the same. [Also] Valencia, they’re all different. But when kids start out [in various academies], everyone knows how to play left-back, right-back, possession, the technique, chasing balls under pressure, how to receive balls in tight spaces.



“In England, it doesn’t happen. Every club wants to be different. So when they come to play for the national team, it’s different. When we [Spain] come to the national team, we have so much ground in common and obviously we are there to serve the national team.”

Ever since Sir Gareth Southgate revived England’s ability to challenge for honours in 2018, the national team has seemed quite comfortable beating inferior opponents.

The same goes against former powerhouses whose glory days are behind them, such as Germany at Euro 2020 and the Netherlands at Euro 2024.



But upon facing legitimate favourites, like Italy at Euro 2020, France at the 2022 World Cup, Spain in 2024 and Argentina this year, England struggle significantly.

The Three Lions also find themselves switching off after taking the lead, as shown most recently against the Albiceleste.

That reinforces Mendieta’s arguments as he also noticed similar signs in 2018 when England crashed out in the semi-finals against Croatia.

The ex-Lazio and Barcelona star insists the whole system – from the FA to the substitutes – need to understand that “every detail counts a lot” if they want to finally win their first trophy since the 1966 World Cup.

Mendieta added: When you get to that level, every detail counts a lot. It makes a difference between winning and losing.



“So understanding how to play these games, Croatia [at the 2018 World Cup] were just passing the ball, and they [England] could not get the ball. So I think it all comes down to that.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“To the federation and training facilities. It comes down to a country producing players throughout the nation who will then come to the national team and have some common ground.

“You cannot see that reflected in the national team, and you have a German coach [Tuchel] – which obviously doesn’t mean much.”

Sports.title: Alan Shearer fears for future England striker hopes as Harry Kane retirement fears linger after World Cup exit
Sports.content:
ALAN SHEARER is worried about England’s attacking options once Harry Kane’s legs finally go.

Kane – who turns 33 later this month – is England’s top scorer with 85 goals and is set to eclipse ex-goalkeeper Peter Shilton’s record of 125 caps for the Three Lions.



Like the rest of the squad, he cut a devastated figure as Thomas Tuchel’s troops lost 2-1 to Argentina in the World Cup semi-finals in Atlanta.

And, despite an incredible scoring spree for Bayern Munich last season, Kane will be approaching his 35th birthday by the time the European Championships take place across England, Ireland, Scotland and Wales in 2028.



There is a good chance he will not be the talisman for the nation when the World Cup takes place in 2030 across three continents.

And Shearer – the Premier League’s top scorer with 260 goals – is concerned about the replacements for Kane for when he does call it a day.

Speaking in his role as a Betfair ambassador, Shearer, 55, said: “The one area of concern for me would be at the minute if Harry is not in the Euro 2028 squad.

“Who are the centre forwards going to be for England?

“Unfortunately that looks like a difficult question to answer at the moment.

“I think that would be a concern because clearly, he can’t go on forever. And another two years on, he’s going to be touching 35.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

“Whether he’ll still be at the level or not, I think without doubt he’ll get the appearance record for England and deserves it.

“He’s been a giant for England. But whether he can go again in the future I am not sure.

“I don’t think he will be around in four years’ time, but whether he can go again in two years, then we’ll have to see. That might be a different matter.

“He knows his body better than most. But he looked sharp in this World Cup, to be honest.

“I know we didn’t see the best of him. He didn’t produce in the game against Argentina, but up until then, I thought he more than played his part and he had some brilliant moments.”



Shearer has been criss-crossing the United States and Mexico to cover England matches for the BBC.

The former Newcastle striker is not jumping on the ‘Tuchel out bandwagon’ despite the semi-final exit.

And he believes the German coach – who has the full backing of the FA – will learn from the “costly error” he made with his substitutes in the defeat last Wednesday to Lionel Messi’s Argentina.

Shearer said: “I said before the tournament, I wouldn’t have picked the squad that he picked.



“There would have been four, five, maybe six different players in it for me, but that’s fine.

“They got through to a semi-final again. Given his contract, given what has gone on, he’s made an error, a costly error, and it’s hurt us.

“But I do think he can continue to the Euros and hopefully that won’t happen again.

“I hope he accepts that he got it wrong. I guess you always look forward and you learn, no matter how old you are and how successful you’ve been.

“He’ll be hurting, I guess. I don’t think this Argentina team are as good as the one that won the World Cup four years ago.



“A very similar squad, four years older. There was an unbelievable opportunity for us there.

“We worked so hard to get in front and do the hard part. Then to see what happened afterwards, well it without doubt would have hurt the players.

Sports.title: Julian Alvarez transfer deadline date ‘set’ with Arsenal and Barcelona ‘keen on move for Argentina star after World Cup’
Sports.content:
THE Julian Alvarez transfer saga could be done and dusted by the end of the month.

Barcelona are in heavy pursuit of the Atletico Madrid star despite their La Liga rivals insisting he will not leave the club.



Atletico Madrid CEO Gil Marin said: “My opinion is clear, the club’s will is clear, we have made it clear to the player, the agent, the president of Barca.

“We do not want to transfer him, we do not accept the offer of 100million euros nor will we accept one of 150 or 200.”



Alvarez reportedly wants a move to the Spanish champions, but tensions between Barcelona and Atletico have played out over social media since the pursuit became public.

Arsenal are a distant second in the race, but reports have suggested that if Alvarez was to move, Atletico would prefer to sell him to a team outside of Spain.



And Barca are starting to accept that they won’t be able to sign the striker unless he makes a firm stand against the board.

Alvarez has already stated Barcelona would be a dream move for him and he thinks it’s best for all parties to make it happen.

But Barcelona believe the Argentine needs to take a firmer stance – perhaps similar to Alexander Isak last summer – if the move is to materialise.

And they have now set a deadline of July 31 for the move to happen.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

President Joan Laporta has insisted while they do want Alvarez, they are prepared to walk away if they have to.

He said: “We have made a very significant offer; if they are willing to accept it, fantastic, but it won’t be unlimited. We have to make a decision. Whether we maintain the offer or not depends on how these last two weeks of July unfold.

“The player has spoken out, and that’s why the issue is still open. It’s clear that the player wants a change of scenery, and we are prepared to welcome him. We’ll see how it all unfolds.

“Deco is doing a great job. He’s brought in [Karim] Adeyemi, whom we’ll sign next week . He’s working very efficiently and discreetly, as it should be done.



“Obviously, if the Julian deal falls through, we have alternatives.”

If there is no progress, Barcelona will turn their attentions elsewhere with plenty of money at their disposal.

According to Atletico president Enrique Cerezo, that’s exactly what they will have to do.

He said: “Joan Laporta is a good friend, he’s a great president, and he knows very well, as do all of you, where Julian Alvarez will be playing next year.”

Sports.title: Chelsea ‘told to cough up £55million for France World Cup star, 26, who is set for rare start against England TONIGHT’
Sports.content:
CHELSEA target Maxence Lacroix is valued at £55million by Crystal Palace, according to reports.

The Blues want to recruit the France international as they look to bolster their defence for new boss Xabi Alonso.



Lacroix, 26, has impressed in the Premier League since moving to Selhurst Park from Wolfsburg two years ago.

According to The Times, the centre-back has indicated that he would like to leave Palace for a new challenge this summer – but he won’t come cheap.



Having seen Jan Paul van Hecke and Luka Vuskovic move for more than £50m apiece, Palace believe that Lacroix should command at least £55m.

The in-demand star has three years remaining on his £60,000-a-week contract, giving Palace some leverage.



Lacroix is set to start for France against England in the World Cup third place play-off, in the absence of injured Arsenal defender William Saliba.

He could come up against his former Palace centre-back partner Marc Guehi, who was sold to Manchester City in January.

Chelsea, meanwhile, want to sell Axel Disasi permanently – having loaned him to both Aston Villa and West Ham in the last 18 months.

Former Palace loanee Trevoh Chalobah could also depart, with Italian side Como keen.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

Chelsea have already bolstered their back line with the £43m addition of Marco Palestra from Atalanta.

Palace, meanwhile, have brought in former Barcelona star Oscar Mingueza on a free transfer.

And they are also keen on Chrislain Matsima from Augsburg.

Pierre Sage’s side began their pre season campaign earlier today, beating Swindon 5-1 behind closed doors.

Sports.title: Arsenal transfer target told he wouldn’t get into Man Utd team in brutal verdict
Sports.content:
Arsenal transfer target told he wouldn’t get into Man Utd team in brutal verdict

Arsenal are looking to strengthen their squad after winning the Premier League, but one of their top transfer targets have been told he wouldn't be good enough for Manchester United's XI right now

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta and Michael Carrick have both been linked with the same player (Image: Zohaib Alam, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Former Manchester United forward Dwight Yorke does not believe Bruno Guimaraes is a top level midfielder. Arsenal have been pursuing a move for the Newcastle United ace, who has made it clear he wants to join the champions.

‌



The Brazilian international recently informed the Magpies he is looking for an exit from St. James' Park, and has reportedly agreed a five-year deal with the Gunners. Arsenal have already seen a £55million bid for the 29-year-old be rejected by the Magpies.

‌



United are also believed to be considering a move for Guimaraes, who has been at the club since January 2021, when he arrived from Lyon. Despite Mikel Arteta believing he would be an emphatic addition to his Premier League title winning side, Yorke does not believe Guimaraes is good enough for United.

‌



Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

The 54-year-old, who wore the red shirt between 1998 and 2002, told Boyle Sports: "I don't know about Bruno Guimaraes. I'm not sure he has been that impressive. I watched him play for Brazil at the World Cup and he's not convinced me.

"I think he's good. He's shown that at Newcastle United. He's got a good work ethic. I understand the value of that. But is that what you're paying for when you sign a player to come to Manchester United? A good work ethic?

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"He's a solid player and maybe he's good enough to get into a team at the level Manchester United should be at but is going to take them to another level? Will Bruno Guimaraes put United any closer to the Premier League title?

"If so, he's a good signing. But he doesn't excite me. I'm not seeing him picking up a ball and boom, sending over one of those diagonal passes or cutting defenders apart with one ball. I just don't see that quality from him.

‌



View 3 Images Bruno Guimaraes missed a penalty when Norway lost to Brazil in the World Cup round of 16 (Image: MAURO PIMENTEL, AFP via Getty Images)

"That's why his performances for Brazil worried me. He was just another solid player in that team. They're all solid players. I'm not saying he's not a good player but is that where United are at now? Just buying players because they're solid?

"Bring me players that are going to make us superior! I'm not so sure that's Bruno Guimaraes. The World Cup was an opportunity for him to tell the world there's a reason why a team like Manchester United are going to be after me, and he's come up short, in my opinion."

‌



View 3 Images Guimaraes is being strongly pursued by Arsenal (Image: GLYN KIRK, AFP via Getty Images)

Yorke also suggested that clubs would be better placed to secure Lille starlet Ayyoub Bouaddi, who put in a stunning World Cup display for Morocco.

At just 18 years old, the midfielder proved on football's grandest stage that he can hold his own against the most experienced professionals, sparking widespread interest from a host of clubs.

‌



While Arsenal are also linked with Bouaddi, they face stiff competition from the likes of Manchester City, Real Madrid, Paris Saint-Germain and Liverpool in the battle for his signature.

Lille have further set a price tag of around £84m for the youngster, determined to retain his services for at least one more season.

Man Utd player ratings vs Wrexham as Andrey Santos impresses and young trio stand out in loss

Manchester United kicked off their pre-season preparations as they took on Wrexham at the Olympic Stadium in Helsinki, Finland.

View 3 Images Manchester United took on Wrexham in pre-season action on Saturday. (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Pre-season has started for Manchester United as they took on Championship side Wrexham at the Olympic Stadium in Helsinki. Sam Smith's first half goal gave Wrexham a 1-0 win.

‌



Wrexham had a couple of early chances as they caught United off guard with their high press, but United stood firm under the pressure. Things settled down more after the first 10 minutes or so, but they still had to be wary of the counter-attack.

‌



Michael Carrick's team struggled to deal with longer balls from the Championship side. But, it was from a throw-in that Wrexham took the lead. The ball made its way past the six-yard box, where an unmarked Smith was there to put it in an empty net.

‌

United made 11 changes at half-time, with the team for the second 45 having a much more youthful look as the young players were given a chance to impress Carrick. Despite the youthfulness of the squad, United looked more comfortable on the ball, with Wrexham also making several changes at the half-time break.

Wrexham did have the chance to double their lead, though, with United having Radak Vitek to thank for keeping the score at 1-0.

Sports.title: Spain and Argentina World Cup final training plans rocked by electrical thunderstorms
Sports.content:
Spain and Argentina World Cup final training plans rocked by electrical thunderstorms

Spain meet Argentina in the World Cup final at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on Sunday but neither were able to train on Saturday

View 2 Images Neither Spain or Argentina were able to train before the World Cup final

Spain were forced to cancel their final training session before the World Cup final.

‌



La Roja were due to train at New York Red Bull's former base, Melanie Lane in Whippany on Saturday morning but the session was initially delayed due to electrical thunderstorms in New Jersey.

‌



Reluctantly, the Royal Spanish Football Federation then decided to cancel training altogether due to lightning in the area. It's understood Spain's players were set to partake in an extended gym session inside instead.

‌



Boss Luis de la Fuente does not have any injury issues to worry about after confirming on Friday that Lamine Yamal will be fit to feature.

Yamal has been suffering with a thigh issue after taking a blow that won Spain a penalty in their 2-0 semi-final triumph over France on Tuesday.

Spain star Aymeric Laporte calls out Argentina over England World Cup antics READ MORE :

Meanwhile, Argentina's training plans were also disrupted. The reigning champions were initially due to take to the field at the Red Bulls Performance Center in Morristown, New Jersey at 11:30am local time but the session was also delayed due to lightning strikes.

‌



The AFA then rescheduled the session for 12:15pm local. The players did eventually emerge on the rain-soaked turf.

Lionel Scaloni had already revealed that he was frustrated with the time FIFA had instructed Argentina to train on Friday, explaining: "Today they forced us to train at a time we didn't want, but with the conference and everything, we had to do a strange, quick training session, and we could hardly try anything out."

View 2 Images Spain had to cancel their session in New Jersey due to storms

‌



Spain head coach De la Fuente is relishing the challenge against an opponent that he respects greatly: "Just being in a final is a privilege. I'm not one for cliches. The important thing is to be there. I'd sign up to lose a World Cup final every year.

"That's how important it is. And on top of that, having the chance to fight for the win. You have to enjoy it. Against an opponent who has been outstanding ever since Scaloni took over."

Scaloni was actually mentored by his opposite number during his FIFA Pro License Coaching course.

Kylian Mbappe’s private life from dating trans model to hooking up with team-mate's ex

Kylian Mbappe has been one of the standout performers at the World Cup despite France's poor semi-final elimination

View 5 Images Kylian Mbappe has shone at this summer's World Cup with eight goals (Image: RONALDO SCHEMIDT / AFP via Getty Images)

France may have missed out on a place in the World Cup final, but Kylian Mbappe still has plenty to play for when Les Bleus face England in Saturday’s third-place play-off. The Real Madrid superstar remains locked with Lionel Messi on eight goals in the race for the tournament’s Golden Boot and will be determined to finish on a high after France’s semi-final defeat to Spain.

‌



Watching on from home is expected to be rumoured girlfriend Ester Exposito, the glamorous Spanish actress who has been linked with Mbappe since the start of the year. The Netflix star has become the latest famous name to be associated with the France captain, whose colourful dating history has attracted almost as much attention as his exploits on the pitch.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



The blonde star is a familiar face across Spain, having shot to fame in the hugely popular Netflix series 'Elite'. She has racked up more than 24 million followers on Instagram, where she regularly treats her fans to an array of stylish and eye-catching photos.

The pair set tongues wagging in February after being spotted together in Madrid in late February, followed by another sighting in Paris in early March – though neither has publicly confirmed their relationship. Expositio is merely the latest in a string of names to be linked with Mbappe, who has enjoyed a colourful personal life away from the game.

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

Sports.title: Youri Tielemans transfer clause Man Utd used kept secret from Aston Villa staff
Sports.content:
Youri Tielemans transfer clause Man Utd used kept secret from Aston Villa staff

Manchester United have completed the signing of Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa in a £35million deal, with the Belgian midfielder's fee catching some off guard

View 2 Images Youri Tielemans signed for Manchester United (Image: Manchester United, Manchester United via Getty Images)

The release clause that saw Manchester United prise Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa was not widely known. Even a key figure involved in brokering the deal that saw Villa sign Tielemans was unaware of its existence, according to The Athletic.

‌



Manchester United agreed a £35million transfer for the Belgian midfielder, which sees a substantial profit for the Midlands club who signed him on a free transfer. Tielemans has put pen to paper on a five-year contract at Old Trafford and brings Premier League experience to the Red Devils, with the midfielder having made 244 appearances in the competition.

‌



The former Leicester star comes on board as part of United's midfield overhaul alongside Andrey Santos from Chelsea. The Belgium skipper completed the switch swiftly, as the club pulled out of a proposed deal for Atalanta's Ederson.

‌



Despite his eagerness to make the switch to United, Tielemans was determined that negotiations were conducted above board. After being made aware of their interest, the 29-year-old was reported to be insistent on speaking with manager Unai Emery before entering into any discussions.

Tielemans has been touted as a United target on several previous occasions, but only now have the circumstances aligned to make a move possible. Even at this stage, Villa were keen to keep him at the club, yet for the player himself, the decision was straightforward.

JJ Gabriel dealt Man Utd blow ahead of Wrexham pre-season clash READ MORE :

Following the completion of the deal, Tielemans said: "It's hard to describe just how proud I am to join Manchester United. Signing for such a special club feels incredible, it is the culmination of years of dedication since I first fell in love with football.

‌



"I have had the privilege of experiencing success in the game and it has only increased my determination to achieve more.

"The ambition from everyone at the club is extremely clear; we are all determined to push for the biggest trophies over the coming years."

View 2 Images Youri Tielemans joined Manchester United after the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

United's director of football Jason Wilcox added: "Youri has consistently been one of the most outstanding midfielders in the Premier League throughout the past seven years. He has all of the technical qualities, as well as the ambition and mentality, to thrive at Manchester United.

"Youri's consistency is exceptional, and he will add further composure, creativity and leadership to our squad. We are delighted to welcome a player of his influence and experience, both on the pitch and within the dressing room, as we continue to build a team ready to challenge for the biggest honours."

Sports.title: McIlroy slams 'performative' DeChambeau for 'holding The Open hostage'
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy has issued a scathing attack on Bryson DeChambeau over his 'performative' behaviour and ‘holding the tournament hostage’ during his rules fiasco at The Open.

DeChambeau appeared to have carded a four-under 66 at Royal Birkdale on Friday evening to move within a shot of the halfway lead, only to be involved in a lengthy rules dispute with R&A officials.

The two-time major champion was adjudged to have improved the line of his swing in long grass at the par-four fifth, resulting in a two-shot penalty and dropping him three strokes behind halfway leader Lucas Herbert.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bryson DeChambeau was given a two-shot penalty after inadvertently improving his lie in thick rough on the fifth hole

DeChambeau returned to the course to contest his decision and continued to defend his case in the recorders area, with the decision not being confirmed for nearly 80 minutes after he walked off the 18th green.

"Late night for everyone," said McIlroy. "I won't pretend to be up here and defend Bryson. I'm not particularly fond of him. I think a lot of it's performative. I think a lot of it's for attention.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player David Howell says Bryson DeChambeau showed no due care or attention when standing behind the ball before his shot

"To hold the tournament hostage like that, and to have all of us, players, volunteers, everyone waiting on him to depart, I didn't feel like it was a great look."

Tee times for Saturday's third round weren't released until nearly 11pm due to the delay, labelled a 'joke' by Marco Penge and questioned by Justin Thomas on social media, with DeChambeau going to the range post-round before declining interviews.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Grant Moir, R&A referee, explains why Bryson DeChambeau was handed a two-shot penalty

DeChambeau said on social media that he was 'disappointed' and 'didn't agree' with the ruling, which dropped him back to tied-fifth, although McIlroy insisted that R&A officials made the correct decision.

"I was watching it live," McIlroy added. "I was up in the players' lounge watching it with a few other players, and as soon as he made the step into the ball, we all sort of looked at each other and were like 'that didn't seem right'.

Sports.title: Johanna Walsh steps up to deliver effortless Irish Oaks success
Sports.content:
Johanna Walsh proved a more than able deputy for her stablemate Thundering On as she ran out a facile winner of the Juddmonte Irish Oaks.

Thundering On blew her rivals away in the Oaks at Epsom last month and while she had since proved no match for top-class older mare Estrange in the Pretty Polly Stakes, she was well fancied to complete a Classic double on home soil, only to be declared a non-runner on Saturday morning.

Despite her absence, Joseph O'Brien still fired a twin assault in his bid for an Oaks double of his own, with Johanna Walsh - runner-up to the reopposing Earth Shot in the Ribblesdale Stakes at Royal Ascot last month - joined by the unbeaten Rebel Moon.

Johanna Walsh was a well backed 7-2 shot in the hands of Dylan Browne McMonagle and after tracking the Ballydoyle pacemakers into the home straight, she opened up from two furlongs down to leave the chasing pack trailing in her wake, with four lengths the winning margin.

David Menuisier's French Oaks third Inis Mor was best of the rest in second ahead of Sparan Nua in third and Rebel Moon in fourth.

O'Brien said: "It was a huge performance from the filly and I thought Dylan gave her a fantastic ride because he controlled the whole race and had a very willing partner. He felt like he'd be able to do that from a mid-pack position and he really did.

"She came on the bridle between the three and the two (furlong markers). We knew that she'd love the fast ground and we felt like she was in good shape coming here.

"It's really special to win a Classic here in Ireland. This is what we are in the game for and this is why we do what we do.

"We'll enjoy today. She's had a busy first part of the season. We'll probably give her a little freshen up now and focus on an autumn campaign."

Of Thundering On, the trainer added: "She'll be back in the autumn. She's an exciting filly, it's a pity we didn't get to see her here today but we'll have her back for the autumn."

McMonagle said: "That was unreal. She's a filly with a lot of gears and when I pushed the button she put the race to bed in a couple of strides, so it wasn't a bad substitute!

"I didn't think there was a whole lot between this filly and Rebel Moon. This one has more experience and I think Rebel Moon is going to be open to more improvement towards the backend of the year, but this one was cherry-ripe for the day and she was unbelievable. It was push button stuff so a big well done to everyone.

"We had three good fillies in the race and every one had their chance of winning. Thundering On is obviously a little bit special, it's hard to know what she would have done the way this one performed, but thankfully the way it worked out it was all in my favour."

Celeron powers to Railway Stakes success

Celeron bounced back from Royal Ascot disappointment with a runaway victory in the GAIN Railway Stakes at the Curragh.

Michael O'Callaghan's juvenile had made a big impression on his racecourse debut at this venue in early June and as a result connections travelled to the Royal meeting with hopes ahead of his tilt at the Windsor Castle Stakes.

Unfortunately a slow start put him on the back foot from the start, however, and he never threatened to land a telling blow, but he showed his true colours back on home soil.

A 7-2 shot in the hands of Oisin Murphy, Celeron quickened up to take over the lead racing inside the last of six furlongs and passed the post with three lengths in hand over Tribeca. Aidan O'Brien's 11-10 favourite Confucius was only third.

Image: 18-7-26 Curragh..Celeron and Oisin Murphy win the GAIN Railway Stakes (Group 2)..Healy Racing Photo

O'Callaghan said: "Any day you can get Oisin is a bonus - he gave him a great ride.

"I was a little bit worried about the trip today - six furlongs looks like his minimum now. He won his maiden over six furlongs but when this horse steps up to seven furlongs or even a mile, we'll see the best of him.

"Oisin said today it was only because of his class he got through. He found the pace mid-race a little bit hot, but he said the horse has plenty of class and took plenty of pulling up.

"His next race will be over seven furlongs and he could be a horse to go a mile next May."

Cover Up battles gamely to land Sapphire Stakes

Cover Up finished with a flourish to lead home a British one-two-three-four in the Tulfarris Hotel And Golf Resort Sapphire Stakes at the Curragh.

Simon and Ed Crisford's winner struck gold twice in Dubai during the winter and was last seen finishing in midfield in the King Charles III Stakes at Royal Ascot.

A 7-1 shot dropping down to Group Two level in Ireland, the six-year-old looked flat out at the halfway stage under James Doyle, but with the near side rail to help he kept himself in the fight and was doing his best work at the finish as he got up to score by three-quarters of a length.

Image: 18-7-26 Curragh..Cover Up and James Doyle win the Tulfarris Hotel And Golf Resort Sapphire Stakes (Group 2)..Healy Racing Photo

Dave Loughnane's Partisan Hero was second ahead of Robert Cowell's Jakajaro in third and the George Boughey-trained 5-2 favourite Rosy Affair in fourth.

Ed Crisford said: "He's a really wonderful horse to have in the stable, a high-quality sprinter who did well in Dubai.

"Ascot was the aim but he just got no run really, running into the back of horses.

"We thought this track would suit him well. I was a little bit worried because there was no rain and we always thought he liked to get his toe in a bit, but he handled it super and finished really well."

Cover Up will now return to Group One company, with an appearance at York next month on the agenda.

Crisford added: "We'll run in the Nunthorpe and maybe come back here for the Flying Five."

Sports.title: Antonelli beats Verstappen to Belgian GP pole
Sports.content:
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli beat Max Verstappen to pole position for the Belgian Grand Prix after a tense conclusion to qualifying at Spa-Francorchamps.

Antonelli dominated practice but Lando Norris was on provisional pole after the first Q3 runs only for Antonelli and Verstappen to topple the McLaren driver.

Verstappen benefitted from a big slipstream with the help of Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar, who starts at the back due to a power unit change, but missed out on pole to Antonelli by 0.317s.

Antonelli absorbed the pressure of being favourite with a strong final lap and has a big opportunity to extend his 25-point lead in the Drivers' Championship over George Russell, who qualified fourth and was half a second down on his team-mate.

Norris will start 13th because of a 10-grid place penalty for exceeding his control electronics allowance - an element of the power unit - so Russell will move up to third on the grid.

Russell has been struggling all weekend, strangely losing time on the straights - which may be down to his driving style in the corners - and will hope the long, flat-out run after the first corner will give him a chance to perhaps challenge Antonelli and Verstappen for the lead on what should be a thrilling first lap when the lights go out at 2pm on Sunday (build-up from 12.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The thrilling end to the Belgian GP qualifying

Ferrari will be disappointed as Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton will start fourth and fifth, making it difficult for the Scuderia to continue their recent winning form.

Hamilton crashed heavily in final practice but Ferrari were able to change his suspension, floor and gearbox in time for qualifying with no impact on the car's performance.

British teenager Arvid Lindblad had his best qualifying in eighth as he continues his impressive rookie season, with McLaren's Oscar Piastri in seventh and Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto in ninth.

Belgian GP Qualifying: Top 10 1) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



2) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



3) Lando Norris, McLaren*



4) George Russell, Mercedes



5) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



6) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



7) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



8) Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls



9) Gabriel Bortoleto, Audi



10) Isack Hadjar, Racing Bulls**



*10-grid place penalty for exceeding control electronics allocation



**starts at the back for exceeding several power unit elements allocation

How Antonelli delivered under serious pressure

Antonelli has seen his championship lead cut over the last three rounds, primarily due to misfortune of car unreliability, but it has still felt like he's got momentum over closest title rivals Russell and Hamilton due to his searing pace. He has been flying all weekend at Spa-Francorchamps but left it late to deliver in qualifying.

Norris delivered a spectacular lap on the first runs in Q3 to pip Antonelli by 0.039s but felt he got everything out of his car. Nevertheless, he was on provisional pole and a red flag for gravel on the track only built the tension ahead of the last runs.

Due to Hadjar knowing he was starting at the back, Red Bull elected to use him to tow Verstappen in Q3 through the largely flat-out final sector into the last chicane.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen praises the efforts of Isack Hadjar after the Frenchman provided a tow for his Red Bull teammate at the end of Belgian GP qualifying, helping him secure P2 on the grid

They did not quite get it right on the first run but perfected it for the second run as Verstappen got a huge increase in speed behind his team-mate to get onto the front row - something he thought was not possible without the slipstream.

"It was definitely helping me otherwise I would not be standing here. Otherwise I think I would be P6 or something," said Verstappen.

But Verstappen was only briefly on pole as Antonelli made a front wing change that paid off as he delivered a superb lap to beat the field by over three tenths.

"It was not a very straightforward session, the track changed a lot. But we were able to improve lap by lap and to bring home pole, which was nice," said Antonelli.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli joins Sky Sports' Karun Chandhok at the SkyPad to analyse the Italians' pole-setting lap at the Belgian Grand Prix

Norris overpushed and went wide at the Fagnes Chicane - the scene where Hamilton and Pierre Gasly suffered major crashes in practice - so aborted his run, but it was still enough to qualify third.

No one else was in the pole fight and Russell in particular will be scratching his head at his pace deficit to Antonelli, which has been a theme all weekend.

The Mercedes driver may be looking over his shoulder at the Ferraris on Sunday, unless Antonelli falters at the front.

Ferrari's expectations of the track layout - which has a high reliance on a strong engine - would not suit them.
